info.title: Argus API
info.description: Self-hosted uptime monitoring. Automation uses an API token (Settings → Access → API tokens) sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or `X-Api-Token: <token>`. The browser UI uses a session cookie against the same endpoints.

tags.name: status
tags.description: Public status pages, badges and feeds (no auth)

tags.name: reporting
tags.description: SLA reporting and the audit log

get.summary: List monitors with their current state

delete.summary: Delete a monitor and its history

post.summary: Run a check now and wait for the result
post.description: Queues a check for the probe and waits up to the monitor's timeout plus five seconds. The result is not stored as a regular check.

applied.description: False when the monitor is paused, so the result did not change its state

504.description: The probe did not run the check in time

post.summary: Run a transaction once without saving it
post.description: Validates the body exactly as a save would and runs it from the API server, not from remote probes. With monitor_id, secrets sent blank use that monitor's stored values. Limited to 10 runs a minute per user.

200.description: The run finished; success says whether it passed

400.description: Invalid transaction, or not a transaction

post.summary: Add monitors from a pasted list
post.description: One monitor per line: a URL becomes an HTTP check, host:port a TCP check, and anything else is pinged. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. Each line is validated like the full form; lines that fail or are already watched are skipped with a reason. At most 50 lines.

200.description: What was created and what was skipped

400.description: Nothing to add, or more than 50 lines

post.summary: Preview when a cron schedule fires
post.description: Answers 200 with an error message for an invalid schedule, so a form can validate as it is typed.

200.description: The next three times, or an error

minutes.description: 1–10080 to mute for that long, 0 to unmute, -1 to mute until unmuted

post.description: Only a monitor that is currently down can be acknowledged.

minutes.description: 0 acknowledges until the monitor recovers; 1–10080 for a fixed window

post.summary: Act on up to 250 monitors at once

get.summary: Latency and failures over a window

200.description: Raw checks or rollups, depending on the window

get.summary: Uptime against each monitor's SLO target

get.description: Call this from a cron or backup job. A push monitor goes down when it is not called within its interval.
Admin only, and recorded in the audit log. Contains every stored credential in clear; prefer the encrypted form.

post.summary: Download a backup encrypted with a passphrase
post.description: Admin only. scrypt and AES-256-GCM. Import it with the same passphrase.

post.summary: Import an Argus export or an Uptime Kuma backup

passphrase.description: Required when data is an encrypted export

200.description: Counts of imported and skipped monitors

400.description: Unreadable file, or a missing or wrong passphrase

get.description: Each step is read from the data: monitors, channels, a delivered channel test, and status pages.

test_alert_at.description: When a channel test was last delivered

smtp_ready.description: Whether an email channel would deliver

test_alert_at.description: When a channel test was last delivered

smtp_ready.description: Whether an email channel would deliver

post.description: Creates a published page listing every monitor, under a free slug made from the organization's name.

bearerAuth.description: An API token from Settings → Access

target.description: Host, URL, host:port, domain, or label, depending on the type. For a transaction it is set from the first step's URL.

retries.description: Consecutive failures before the monitor is down

latency_threshold_ms.description: Above this, an up monitor is reported slow

channel_ids.description: Null uses every channel; an empty array silences the monitor

probe_node_ids.description: Where the check runs. 0 is this server; empty means this server alone. Push and group monitors are always local.

confirm_locations.description: How many locations must see the monitor down before it is down, from 1 to the number of locations. Locations whose probe has stopped reporting drop out of the count.

MonitorConfig.description: Type-specific options. Secrets are never returned by the API.

auth_password.description: Stored encrypted when ARGUS_SECRET_KEY is set; never returned

expect_value.description: Expected DNS answer (substring for TXT) or database result

warn_days.description: How early a cert or domain expiry warning fires; default 14 for cert, 30 for domain

tls_mode.description: Mail monitors; redis accepts none or tls

database.description: Database name for postgres and mysql

query.description: Statement returning one value (postgres, mysql) or a read command (redis). Redis commands are limited to reads.

steps.description: Transaction monitors: requests run in order with one cookie jar. The first failing step fails the check.

secrets.description: Transaction monitors: named values steps use as {{secret.name}}. Encrypted at rest; reads return the names with empty values, and sending an empty value on update keeps the stored one.

schedule.description: Push monitors: a five-field cron expression (or @daily, @hourly, @weekly) for when the ping is expected. The interval becomes one minute.

timezone.description: IANA time zone for schedule; UTC when empty

url.description: http or https URL. May use {{name}} and {{secret.name}}.

body.description: Not allowed for GET or HEAD. Content-Type defaults from the body's shape.

keyword.description: Must appear in the response body

path.description: Dotted JSON path (numeric segments index arrays) or a header name

next_ping_at.description: When a scheduled heartbeat is next due

CheckEvidence.description: What the probe saw on the last failure

curl.description: A curl command that reproduces the check

steps.description: Transaction monitors: each step run, up to and including the one that failed

dest.description: Addresses for email; a webhook URL for slack, discord, teams, ntfy and webhook; an integration key (optionally suffixed @eu) for pagerduty and opsgenie; <bot token>:<chat id> for telegram
